TABLE 3.2 Energy Production from the Metabolism of Macronutrients with B Vitamin Catalysts 
B vitamins must have macronutrients (carbohydrates, fat, and protein) available for energy production. Taking a 
vitamin supplement instead of a balanced meal does not provide a substrate for coenzyme action. Instead, 
obtaining vitamins through foods is preferred. Remember that none of the other B vitamins can cover a deficiency of 
another. 
Choline, Biotin, and Folate 
Other water-soluble substances that are less known include choline, biotin, and folate. Choline is an essential 
nutrient, not classified as a vitamin or a mineral, and is naturally present in food. Choline is often grouped with the B 
vitamins because it has similar functions. Vitamin research continues to improve classification, and in 2022 for the 
first time, a set amount, or Daily Value, for choline intake was included in the Daily Values (DVs), the list of all 
vitamins and minerals needed (FDA, 2022a). This nutrient is a source of methyl groups needed for many steps in
